research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current July 2026 GOV.UK/MHCLG and Planning Inspectorate National Infrastructure Planning guidance checked on 25 July 2026. Pre-application, acceptance, examination, decision, DCO preparation, rights of entry, EIA/HRA, fees and post-consent changes remain at their published procedural and statutory scope. They are not parcel planning permission, compulsory-acquisition outcome, project approval probability, delivered infrastructure or Future Growth score accuracy.

source_facts.fact: As of 24 July 2026 the portal identifies the July 2026 guidance suite in effect for key NSIP stages and related Planning Act 2008 processes.
source_facts.gate: A guidance page being in effect is not a DCO decision for any particular project.

source_facts.fact: The July 2026 pre-application guidance covers preparation, engagement, project programme and application readiness and notes NSIP BNG becomes mandatory from 2 November 2026.
source_facts.gate: Pre-application activity is not application acceptance, examination or consent.

source_facts.fact: Acceptance determines whether an application can proceed to examination; after acceptance relevant-representation periods are subject to statutory/publicity requirements.
source_facts.gate: Accepted for examination does not mean development consent has been granted.

source_facts.fact: The Examining Authority controls the examination within the statutory framework and can consider written representations, hearings and limited application changes.
source_facts.gate: Examination participation or a change request is not the Secretary of State's final DCO decision.

source_facts.fact: Current pre-application guidance states section 53 authorised entry generally requires at least 14 days' notice to owners or occupiers.
source_facts.gate: Rights-of-entry authorisation is not acquisition of title or development consent.

source_facts.fact: Planning Inspectorate guidance distinguishes EIA consultation and HRA screening, appropriate assessment and derogation stages within NSIP preparation and examination.
source_facts.gate: Environmental assessment process steps are not project consent or proof effects are acceptable.

official_measurement_examples.name: July 2026 infrastructure guidance status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The National Infrastructure Planning Guidance Portal states which July 2026 Planning Act guidance is in effect as of 24 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: NSIP BNG future-effective date
official_measurement_examples.fact: July 2026 pre-application guidance states BNG becomes mandatory for NSIPs from 2 November 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 53 entry notice period
official_measurement_examples.fact: July 2026 pre-application guidance describes at least 14 days' notice before authorised section 53 entry to land.

official_measurement_examples.name: Acceptance status semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: Acceptance allows an application to proceed toward examination and is not a grant of development consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Relevant representation period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Acceptance guidance says the representation deadline must be no less than 28 days, or 30 days for EIA development, after required publicity/notices are received and should normally not exceed six weeks.

official_measurement_examples.name: Examination change request semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: July 2026 examination guidance treats changes after acceptance as exceptional and subject to examination/procedural considerations.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026/27 NSIP fee publication
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current application-fee guidance applies charges from 1 April 2026 for pre-application and application-processing services.

official_measurement_examples.name: HRA stages
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current NSIP HRA advice distinguishes screening, appropriate assessment and derogation stages where applicable.

core_rules: NSIP guidance in effect is not a project DCO decision
pre-application engagement is not application acceptance
application preparation is not examination acceptance
application submitted is not application accepted
application accepted is not development consent granted
relevant representation is participation evidence not project approval or refusal
interested-party status is not a land-right determination
examination start is not project consent
examination recommendation is distinct from the Secretary of State decision where applicable
decision-making guidance is not a decision on a specific project
DCO grant is distinct from discharge of requirements during implementation
DCO grant is not proof construction has commenced
DCO grant is not proof infrastructure has been delivered
post-consent material-change application is not an approved change
material-change fee payment is not approval of the requested change
pre-application service tier is not an approval probability
application fee amount is not a viability conclusion
Planning Inspectorate advice is not legal advice or a binding project decision
local-authority participation does not mean local authority consent has been granted
statement of common ground records positions and does not itself grant consent
draft DCO is not a made DCO
book of reference is not conclusive title determination
land plan is not a Land Registry title plan
compulsory-acquisition request is not compulsory-acquisition authority granted
compulsory-acquisition authority is not evidence acquisition has completed
section 53 right of entry is not acquisition of ownership or permanent access rights
14-day entry notice is procedural and not development consent
linear-project corridor is not a cadastral parcel determination
EIA scoping opinion is not Environmental Statement approval
Environmental Statement submission is not proof environmental effects are acceptable
HRA screening conclusion must remain distinct from appropriate assessment
appropriate assessment is not a derogation decision
HRA derogation cannot be assumed without the applicable legal tests
public-body consultation is not consent from every regulator
deemed consent must not be assumed where separate consent is required
DCO can include or interact with other consents but each mechanism must be evidenced
National Policy Statement support is not automatic project approval
project need policy is distinct from site-specific impacts and alternatives
older pre-application guidance must not override the current July 2026 suite where superseded
current guidance publication date is not a project milestone date
NSIP BNG must not be treated as mandatory before 2 November 2026
future NSIP BNG must not be backdated
BNG obligation is not a DCO grant
fast-track eligibility or service is not guaranteed examination duration
accepted change during examination is not approval of the underlying DCO
legal challenge possibility is not evidence a consent is invalid
NO_DATA must not be converted into no infrastructure-planning constraint
no parcel DCO status compulsory-acquisition outcome or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as project-consent accuracy
